Nul ne doit subir de discrimination du f: No one may be discriminated against, in particular because of their origin, race, sex, age, language, social position, way of life, religious, philosophical or political convictions, or because of a physical, mental or psychological disability.
Le terme \"notamment\" signifie que la l: The word “in particular” means that the list is not exhaustive. Skin colour, ethnicity and migration status are covered. However, this provision does not in itself create an individual right that can be invoked before the courts without further legislation.

Quiconque, publiquement, incite à la hai: Anyone who publicly incites hatred or discrimination against a person or a group of persons because of their race, ethnic origin or religion; anyone who publicly spreads an ideology aimed at systematically demeaning or denigrating such persons...
Condition de publicité : les propos doiv: Condition of publicity: the remarks must have been made in front of third parties (waiting room, corridor, reception). One-to-one remarks are harder to prosecute under this article but may amount to a violation of personality rights (art. 28 Civil Code).

Quiconque, en usant de violence envers u: Anyone who, by using violence against a person or threatening them with serious harm, or by restricting their freedom of action in any other way, compels them to do, not to do or to tolerate an act.
Applicable si un·e soignant·e vous contr: Applicable if a carer forces you to accept a treatment, or if a superior prevents you from reporting discrimination.
Les membres d'une autorité et les foncti: Members of an authority and public officials who, with the intention of gaining an unlawful advantage for themselves or a third party, or of harming another person, abuse the powers of their office shall be punished.
Applicable aux médecins hospitaliers pub: Applicable to public hospital doctors who abuse their power (unjustified PLAFA, systematic discriminatory treatment, falsification of records).
Celui qui subit une atteinte illicite à: Anyone whose personality rights are unlawfully infringed may apply to the court for protection. The infringement is unlawful unless it is justified by the consent of the victim, by an overriding private or public interest, or by law.
Voie civile principale contre la discrim: Main civil route against discrimination. It allows you to ask for: the infringement to stop, a declaration that it is unlawful, and compensation for damage (including non-material harm). There is no need to prove a criminal offence.
Le demandeur peut requérir du juge : qu': The claimant may ask the judge to: prohibit the infringement, if it is imminent; make it cease, if it is still continuing; declare it unlawful, if the disturbance it has caused persists.
Trois types d'actions cumulables. La con: Three types of action that can be combined. A declaration of unlawfulness is important even if the infringement has stopped: it can serve as the basis for a claim for damages.
Celui qui subit une atteinte illicite à: Anyone whose personality rights are unlawfully infringed is entitled to a sum of money as compensation for non-material harm, provided the seriousness of the infringement justifies it and the person responsible has not given satisfaction in another way.
Dommages-intérêts pour la souffrance mor: Damages for the moral suffering caused by discrimination. The amount depends on the seriousness and duration of the infringement. Swiss courts have traditionally been conservative in the amounts awarded.
L'employeur protège et respecte, dans le: The employer must protect and respect the employee's personality in the employment relationship. They take the measures necessary to protect their life, health and personal integrity.
L'hôpital/clinique a l'obligation de pro: Hospitals and clinics must protect their employees from discrimination, including discrimination from patients. Failing to protect them makes the employer liable.
Le congé est abusif lorsqu'il est donné: Notice of termination is abusive when it is given for a reason relating to the other party's personality.
Un licenciement faisant suite à un signa: A dismissal that follows a report of discrimination can be considered abusive. Compensation can be up to 6 months' salary.
Protection des lanceurs d'alerte dans la: Protection of whistleblowers in the public service. Good-faith reports of malfunctions are protected.

Chaque témoignage — positif ou négatif —: Every account — positive or negative — serves four purposes: gathering and structuring experiences from the field, producing publicly available equity indicators, equipping partner associations for their advocacy work, and offering institutions a mirror to improve. Only aggregated data is published — never individual accounts. The institution never sees your report: details that are too specific are automatically generalised before publication.

Oui. CareWatch™ ne vous demande pas votr: Yes. CareWatch™ does not ask for your identity: access is through an anonymous invitation code. Comment empêchez-vous qu'on me reconnais: How do you prevent me from being recognised through my account?
Même sans votre nom, une combinaison de: Even without your name, a combination of precise details (date, small department, rare reason) could in theory make it possible to guess who gave the account. To avoid this, before any publication the moderation team generalises details that are too precise (an automatic k-anonymity check, at least 5 people per combination, is being prepared): some details are generalised — for example, “3 February” becomes “February 2026”, or “Unit 4B of internal medicine” becomes “Internal medicine”. Your full account is kept for statistical analysis, but the data made public is always generalised. This greatly reduces the risk of anyone being able to identify you — even though no system in the world can guarantee 100% absolute anonymity.

Quels mécanismes de sécurité sont en pla: What security mechanisms are in place?
Chiffrement : toutes les communications: Encryption: all communications are encrypted in transit (HTTPS) and the database is encrypted at rest by the host. Anonymity: your identity is not requested; anonymity is part of the design. Hashed personal code: your code is never stored in plain text, only its fingerprint is, and it is required to read, edit or withdraw a report. Compartmentalised access: the database cannot be reached directly from the browser, only controlled functions can, and only the moderation team, bound to secrecy by contract, reads the accounts. Log: every operation (submission, edit, withdrawal) is logged with the report number, without any information about the person. Local check: the postcode is processed only in your browser and is never sent. Protection against abuse: rate limits on the database side. The details are in the privacy policy.

Pourquoi inclure les maladies rares et n: Why include rare and neglected diseases?
Parce que l'accès aux soins spécialisés: Because access to specialised care is a major equity issue. This concerns blood diseases such as sickle cell disease, but also Ehlers-Danlos syndromes (diagnostic delay of 10-15 years), endometriosis (7-10 years), long COVID (roadmap of the Federal Office of Public Health under way, few dedicated consultations), rheumatoid arthritis (often 3+ consultations before diagnosis), adult attention deficit disorder (ADHD) (underdiagnosed in women), autism spectrum disorders (waiting lists of 12-24 months), or chronic fatigue syndrome (almost no specialists in Switzerland). Making this information visible is a first step towards equity. All these consultations are accessible anonymously via CareWatch™.

Quelle est la différence entre inégalité: What is the difference between inequality, inequity and equity?
Une inégalité est une différence mesurab: An inequality is a measurable difference between groups of people, for example life expectancy by income. An inequity is an inequality that could be avoided and that is judged unfair, for example because it comes from the way care is organised. Equity is the goal: that every person receives what they need to be well cared for.
Deux patient·e·s ont le même problème de: Two patients have the same health problem. One is listened to, informed and cared for with respect. The other waits longer or is not understood, for lack of an interpreter. Their need for care is identical. The difference in treatment is an inequity.
Équité ou égalité : est-ce la même chose: Equity or equality: is it the same thing?
Non. L’égalité donne la même chose à tou: No. Equality gives everyone the same thing. Equity gives each person what they need. A person who does not speak French needs an interpreter; another does not. Caring fairly means adapting to each situation.
Inéquité ou iniquité : quel mot est just: Inequity or iniquity: which word is right?
Les deux existent. Iniquité est le mot c: Both exist. Iniquity is the everyday word, in the broad sense of injustice. Inequity is the term used in public health for an avoidable and unjust health inequality. CareWatch uses inequity in this sense.
Comment CareWatch mesure-t-elle l’équité: How does CareWatch measure equity in care?
CareWatch demande aux personnes comment: CareWatch asks people how they were treated: courtesy, respect, quality of care. Verified accounts are combined into an equity index for each institution, from 0 to 100. The higher the index, the more people felt they were treated in the same way as others.
Toute personne ayant vécu ou observé une: Anyone who has experienced or witnessed discrimination in a Swiss healthcare institution: patients, relatives, witnesses or health professionals. Reports are anonymous.
